summary: 0–60, 60–130 mph and 0–100, 100–200 km/h timers on the iDrive 6 screen
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A page under My Vehicle that times the car's acceleration from its speed, read from the engine control unit.

What it does
- Four timers: 0–60 mph, 60–130 mph, 0–100 km/h and 100–200 km/h
- From a standstill the timer starts as the car moves off. For 60–130 mph and 100–200 km/h, drive below the start speed, and the timer starts as the car passes it
- The page shows Ready when the timer is armed and Measuring during a run
- A run ends when the car reaches the end speed. Lifting off, so that the speed drops, or taking longer than 60 seconds stops it with no time
- It keeps the last three times of each timer, and the timer last chosen, across restarts of iDrive. They go when the package is removed
- It only reads the car's speed and sends no commands

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose LaunchDeck.

Good to know
- Time it only where that is legal and safe, such as a closed track. Do not look at the screen during a run
- The time is shown to a hundredth of a second, worked out between the speed readings the engine control unit gives. It is less exact than that, and is no substitute for a GPS timer
- The page is laid out for the screen when the package is installed: 800×480, 960×480, 1280×480 or 1920×720. On a 1440×540 screen the 1280×480 layout is used, as for ShiftDeck, whose 1440×540 layout is reported to be cut off at the right edge. If the screen's size cannot be read, the 1280×480 layout is used too
- Owners report that on some cars the author's apps only get data while a device is plugged into the OBD port
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer accepts only these NBTevo versions: L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T23235J, U19384I, V20153I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- It uses the same iDrive connector as the author's old Exhaust Flap menu, which MHD+ Suite has replaced. If that menu is still on the head unit from a hand install, remove its ExhaustFlap folder first
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps
